meta.title: Turn-assembly stress: values split over turns, fillers, no punctuation (Freya, kit anchors)
meta.why: a7 showed fragments broken across turns; these probe the same class in forms not yet seen (notes/hata-haritasi.md)

scenarios.behaviour: HOW YOU TALK: when you name a payment day, say it in two turns: first 'I could do the twenty...' and stop; in your next turn say '...third, the twenty-third of October.'
HOW YOU TALK: when you accept an amount, repeat it in two turns: first 'Six hundred and...' and stop; in your next turn say '...thirty-seven fifty, yes.'

HOW YOU TALK: give your date of birth in three turns: first only the day ('The fourteenth...'), then only the month ('...of March...'), then only the year ('...nineteen eighty-eight.'). Wait for the caller between the parts.

HOW YOU TALK: when asked for the last four digits of your phone, say the first two digits, then talk about something else in the same turn ('five five... sorry, my dog is barking'), and give the last two digits in your next turn.
HOW YOU TALK: you write like a speech transcript: all lower case, no punctuation at all, not even at the end of a sentence. Say numbers as words.
HOW YOU TALK: you hesitate a lot: 'uh', 'um', 'let me think' inside numbers and dates, like 'nineteen uh eighty-nine' and 'the uh sixteenth'.

HOW YOU TALK: the first time you are asked for a payment day, say 'the twenty-second of October', and in your NEXT turn correct it: 'No wait, I meant the twenty-third.' The corrected day is the one you mean.
HOW YOU TALK: when you say when she can be reached, say it in two turns: 'Tomorrow at...' and stop; then '...eleven in the morning.'
